title: India Can Build 600 MT of Steel. Can It Afford to Move, Fuel and Decarbonise It?
dek: BW Businessworld asks whether India, capable of building 600 MT of steel capacity, can afford the logistics, fuel and decarbonisation that would require.
summary: BW Businessworld examines whether India can afford to move, fuel and decarbonise steel output on a scale of 600 MT. The publisher provided no excerpt, so the article's arguments and figures beyond the headline are not available.
keyFacts: The headline refers to India being able to build 600 MT of steel
whyItMatters: Logistics, energy and raw-material supply, alongside emissions costs, are widely seen as the binding constraints on India's capacity ambitions rather than plant construction itself.
implications: Producers and policymakers could face rising pressure on rail freight, coking coal and gas supply, and on financing low-carbon routes, as capacity expands.
